sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐秘。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: I've been working in radio a long time.
sentences.zh: 我做广播已经很久了。

sentences.en: It's been so long that when I first started out, I did all my interviews on cassette tape, a Marantz PMD-222 to be exact.
sentences.zh: 时间久到我刚开始的时候，所有的采访都是用磁带录的，准确地说，是一台马兰士 PMD-222。

sentences.en: I have a soft spot for cassettes, and that machine in particular.
sentences.zh: 我对磁带情有独钟，对那台机器更是格外偏爱。

sentences.en: But honestly, cassettes never really sounded all that great.
sentences.zh: 但说实话，磁带的声音其实从来没有多好听。

sentences.en: So it was assumed that people would use cassettes for voice recordings, things like reporters using them in the field.
sentences.zh: 所以大家默认磁带是用来录人声的，比如记者在户外采访时会用它。

sentences.en: That's Mark Masters.
sentences.zh: 那是马克·马斯特斯。

sentences.en: He has a new book called High Bias about the history of the cassette.
sentences.zh: 他最近写了一本新书叫《高偏压》，讲述的是磁带的历史。

sentences.en: But because the cassette was so much cheaper and easier to use and portable, a lot of people didn't care so much about the audio quality.
sentences.zh: 但因为磁带便宜得多、用起来更简单而且便于携带，很多人根本不在乎音质。

sentences.en: They just wanted to be able to use something that they could carry around with them.
sentences.zh: 他们只是想能用上一种可以随身携带的东西。

sentences.en: Portability was crucial to the success of the cassette.
sentences.zh: 便携性是磁带成功的关键。

sentences.en: That's 99PI engineer Martin Gonzalez, who knows a thing or two about making things sound good.
sentences.zh: 那是99PI的工程师马丁·冈萨雷斯，他很懂得怎么让声音听起来更好。

sentences.en: Cassettes weren't meant to be as high fidelity as vinyl or reel-to-reels.
sentences.zh: 磁带本来就不是为了达到黑胶或盘式录音带那样的高保真度而设计的。

sentences.en: They were meant to go where those other formats couldn't.
sentences.zh: 它们的使命是去到那些传统格式去不了的地方。

sentences.en: The guy, Lou Ottens, who invented it, his first idea was,
sentences.zh: 发明磁带的那个人叫卢·奥滕斯，他的最初想法是：

sentences.en: I'm going to cut out a block of wood and put it in my pocket and see what feels comfortable,
sentences.zh: 我要削一块木头放进口袋里，看看感觉舒不舒服，

sentences.en: and then I'm going to try to make a cassette player that matches that size.
sentences.zh: 然后我要试着做一台符合这个尺寸的磁带播放器。

sentences.en: Cassettes had another big advantage.
sentences.zh: 磁带还有另一个巨大优势。

sentences.en: They were much easier to record on.
sentences.zh: 用它录音要容易得多。

sentences.en: Before the compact cassette was introduced, recording anything was hard to do.
sentences.zh: 在微型盒式磁带问世之前，录音是一件很难的事。

sentences.en: The equipment was expensive.
sentences.zh: 设备很贵。

sentences.en: The tapes were expensive.
sentences.zh: 磁带很贵。

sentences.en: It was easy to mess it up.
sentences.zh: 而且很容易弄砸。

sentences.en: You kind of had to be sort of a semi-professional to be able to figure any of this out.
sentences.zh: 你得是个半专业人士，才能把这些门道弄明白。

sentences.en: The cassette wasn't really the best format in most ways, but it was the most useful format.
sentences.zh: 在大多数方面，磁带其实并不是最好的格式，但它是最有用的格式。

sentences.en: Mark's book has stories of all kinds of cool scenes that were only made possible by the use of cassettes.
sentences.zh: 马克的书里记录了各种各样酷炫的音乐场景，而这些只有通过使用磁带才得以实现。

sentences.en: Underground, home-recorded, lo-fi indie rap.
sentences.zh: 地下、家庭录制的、低保真的独立说唱。

sentences.en: Early hip-hop blasting from New York City boomboxes.
sentences.zh: 从纽约街头大音箱里轰鸣而出的早期嘻哈。

sentences.en: A treasure trove of Cambodian tapes stashed away in the Oakland Public Library.
sentences.zh: 藏在奥克兰公共图书馆里的一批柬埔寨磁带宝藏。

sentences.en: But there was a chapter that made me realize there's one band that represents the ultimate triumph of the cassette.
sentences.zh: 但其中有一章让我意识到，有一个乐队代表了磁带的终极胜利。

sentences.en: The Grateful Dead.
sentences.zh: 感恩而死乐队。

sentences.en: Look, I am very much not a deadhead.
sentences.zh: 听着，我真的不是他们的死忠粉。

sentences.en: Sorry to our listeners who are, but honestly, up until now, I thought they sucked.
sentences.zh: 向喜欢他们的听众道歉，但说实话，直到现在，我还觉得他们烂透了。

sentences.en: The views expressed herein are solely that of Martin Gonzalez and do not necessarily represent 9MPI, Stitcher, or SiriusXM.
sentences.zh: 本节目表达的观点仅代表马丁·冈萨雷斯个人，并不代表9MPI、Stitcher或SiriusXM。

sentences.en: All right, I've come around a little bit on them, but it's just, I thought I was like, Mr. Cool Music Guy, you know?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我对他们的看法稍微有点转变，但怎么说呢，我以前觉得自己就像是个酷炫音乐达人，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I'm the type of corner you at a party to tell you, actually, my favorite Beach Boys song is the title track from their 1968 album Friends,
sentences.zh: 我就是那种会在派对上把你堵在角落里对你说，其实，我最喜欢的海滩男孩歌曲是他们1968年专辑《朋友》里的同名主打歌，

sentences.en: which I think is probably the apex of their post-Pet Sounds era.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能是他们后《宠物之声》时代的最巅峰。

sentences.en: I thought the dead were for a very different type of person.
sentences.zh: 我以为感恩而死是给完全不同类型的人准备的。

sentences.en: You know the kind, I mean, the ones whose natural habitat is in the parking lots of jam band shows.
sentences.zh: 你知道那种人，我是说，那种天然栖息地在即兴乐队演出的停车场里的人。

sentences.en: Old school hippies, and people my age kind of living an old school hippie life where they're just like in a van,
sentences.zh: 老派嬉皮士，还有像我这个年纪过着老派嬉皮生活的人，他们就住在面包车里，

sentences.en: they're selling burritos, they're white and they have dreadlocks, and they're like wearing no shirt and they're selling mushrooms out of a bag.
sentences.zh: 他们卖卷饼，是白人却留着长长的脏辫，光着膀子从包里兜售迷幻蘑菇。

sentences.en: That's writer and deadhead Sophie Hageny.
sentences.zh: 那是作家兼死忠粉苏菲·哈格尼。

sentences.en: Like a lot of people my age, I got into the dead by osmosis through like my dad,
sentences.zh: 就像我这个年纪的很多人一样，我是通过我爸潜移默化地迷上感恩而死的，

sentences.en: and then it was just like what we had in the car growing up.
sentences.zh: 然后这就成了我们成长过程中车里一直放的音乐。

sentences.en: She knows what people think about dead fans.
sentences.zh: 她很清楚别人是怎么看待死忠粉的。

sentences.en: I approach loving the dead with some amount of self-deprecation just because I'm aware that it's not for everyone to listen to like endless jaMs.
sentences.zh: 我表达对感恩而死的热爱时总会带有一点自嘲，因为我知道不是每个人都能听得下去无休止的即兴演奏。

sentences.en: It can be, I think, really alienating for people who might not have a natural way in.
sentences.zh: 对于那些没有自然接触途径的人来说，这可能会让人觉得非常有距离感。

sentences.en: My way into the dead was through cassettes.
sentences.zh: 我接触感恩而死的途径是通过磁带。

sentences.en: I found it so charming to imagine total strangers, united by their love of this band,
sentences.zh: 我发现这种感觉太迷人了：素不相识的陌生人因为对这个乐队的爱而凝聚在一起，

sentences.en: mailing each other tapes of shows that maybe neither of them even went to.
sentences.zh: 互相邮寄演出磁带，而这些演出他们俩可能都没去过。

sentences.en: But let's rewind the tape back to the beginning of the Grateful Dead.
sentences.zh: 但让我们把磁带倒回感恩而死的起点。

sentences.en: I gotta admit, this kind of rocks.
sentences.zh: 我得承认，这听起来还挺带感的。

sentences.en: What you're hearing is their first known live recording from the January 1966 acid teSt.
sentences.zh: 你听到的是他们目前已知最早的现场录音，来自1966年1月的迷幻派对。

sentences.en: These were happenings thrown by Ken Kesey and his group, the Merry Pranksters.
sentences.zh: 这些是肯·凯西和他的“快乐弄臣”团伙举办的狂欢活动。

sentences.en: Everyone was dosed on LSD, and there were crazy lights and experimental spoken word performances.
sentences.zh: 每个人都嗑了LSD，现场有疯狂的灯光和实验性的语言艺术表演。

sentences.en: The Dead became the de facto house band.
sentences.zh: 感恩而死顺理成章地成了这里的常驻乐队。

sentences.en: They became close with the era's most prolific producer of acid, Owsley Stanley, also known as Bear.
sentences.zh: 他们与那个时代最著名的LSD制造者奥斯利·斯坦利（也被称为“熊”）建立了亲密的关系。

sentences.en: He became the band's patron and first sound engineer, building gigantic high-fidelity PAs for them.
sentences.zh: 他成了乐队的赞助商和第一任音响师，为他们打造了巨大的高保真扩音系统。

sentences.en: Bear started recording the band in his quest to improve the quality of the live sound.
sentences.zh: 为了提升现场音质，“熊”开始录制乐队的表演。

sentences.en: He explained this in this 1991 interview.
sentences.zh: 他在1991年的这次采访中解释了这一点。

sentences.en: My way of doing that was constantly playing the tapes back, listen to the tape, listen to the house, adjust them, listen to the tape, listen to the house.
sentences.zh: 我的做法就是不断地回放磁带，听磁带，听现场场馆的声音，调整它们，再听磁带，再听现场。

sentences.en: After every show, we'd gather in the hotel and play back the night scapes.
sentences.zh: 每次演出结束后，我们都会聚在酒店里回放当晚的录音。

sentences.en: It was always a tape being made.
sentences.zh: 总有源源不断的磁带在制作中。

sentences.en: Throughout the late 1960s, the Dead expanded from their Bay Area roots and started touring nationally.
sentences.zh: 在整个20世纪60年代末，感恩而死走出了湾区本土，开始在全国巡演。

sentences.en: They became a focal point for the counterculture.
sentences.zh: 他们成为了反文化运动的核心。

sentences.en: Their shows were never the same twice.
sentences.zh: 他们的演出从来没有哪两次是相同的。

sentences.en: They would make up the set list as they went, linking songs together with extended improvisations.
sentences.zh: 他们会即兴创作歌单，将不同的歌曲通过超长的即兴演奏串联起来。

sentences.en: The magic of their live shows didn't quite translate into their studio albuMs.
sentences.zh: 他们现场演出的魔力并不能很好地转化为录音室专辑。

sentences.en: They released a few official live albums that were closer to the experience, but...
sentences.zh: 他们发行过几张官方现场专辑，更贴近现场体验，但是……

sentences.en: People really wanted to hear every show, to hear the differences, to hear if there might be something new they're playing, if there might be some new take on an old song.
sentences.zh: 人们真的很想听每一场演出，去听其中的差异，去听他们是不是在演奏什么新东西，对老歌有没有什么全新的演绎。

sentences.en: Intrepid fans would sneak in their own tape recorders and microphones to try to capture the elusive raw magic.
sentences.zh: 勇敢的歌迷会偷偷带上自己的录音机和麦克风，试图捕捉那种难以捉摸的原始魔力。

sentences.en: Early tapers were mostly still using bulky reel-to-reels.
sentences.zh: 早期的录音客大多还在使用笨重的盘式录音带。

sentences.en: When the tape ended, you had to unspool the whole reel to switch tapes.
sentences.zh: 当磁带录完时，你得把整盘带子解开才能换带。

sentences.en: It was a difficult and time-consuming process to do mid-set.
sentences.zh: 在演出间隙做这件事既困难又耗时。

sentences.en: And it wasn't quite accepted yet, so you might have to hide it somewhere.
sentences.zh: 而且当时这种行为还没被完全接受，所以你得把它藏在某个地方。

sentences.en: You might have to try to figure out a way to put a whole reel-to-reel deck, like, in your pants or something.
sentences.zh: 你可能得想办法把一整台盘式录音机塞进裤子里或者别的什么地方。

sentences.en: Mark isn't kidding.
sentences.zh: 马克可不是在开玩笑。

sentences.en: Tapers resorted to elaborate measures, like disguising a mic stand as a leg brace,
sentences.zh: 录音客们采取了各种复杂的手段，比如把麦克风支架伪装成腿部支具，

sentences.en: or burying their gear in the stadium's field a couple days before the show.
sentences.zh: 或者在演出前几天把设备埋在体育场的草坪里。

sentences.en: In those early days, illegal bootlegging was a widespread concern in the music industry.
sentences.zh: 在早期，非法的盗录是音乐行业普遍担忧的问题。

sentences.en: And at first, the band was opposed.
sentences.zh: 起初，乐队是反对的。

sentences.en: The crew would confiscate the tapes or even snip their cables.
sentences.zh: 工作人员会没收磁带，甚至剪断他们的电线。

sentences.en: The taping quickly became so widespread that the band came to a sort of grudging acceptance.
sentences.zh: 但录音风潮迅速蔓延，乐队最终勉强接受了这种做法。

sentences.en: Here's a 1971 recording where guitarist Bob Weir and bassist Phil Lesh poked fun at a taper who was a little too close.
sentences.zh: 这里有一段1971年的录音，吉他手鲍勃·韦尔和贝斯手菲尔·莱什开玩笑调侃了一个离得太近的录音客。

sentences.en: Hey, you down there with the microphone, if you want to get a decent recording, you've got to move back about 40 feet.
sentences.zh: 嘿，下面拿麦克风的那位，如果你想录出像样的声音，你得往后退大约40英尺。

sentences.en: It sounds a lot better back there, believe me.
sentences.zh: 相信我，退后一点听起来好多了。

sentences.en: And Jerry Garcia had taped bluegrass shows when he was younger.
sentences.zh: 杰瑞·加西亚年轻时也录过蓝草音乐演出。

sentences.en: So his philosophy was...
sentences.zh: 所以他的哲学是……

sentences.en: When we're done with it, they can have it, you know.
sentences.zh: 等我们用完了，他们就可以拿去，你知道的。

sentences.en: New York tapers formed clubs to trade recordings.
sentences.zh: 纽约的录音客们组成了俱乐部来交换录音。

sentences.en: They were the first to establish an important principle.
sentences.zh: 他们是最早确立一个重要原则的人。

sentences.en: The tapes couldn't be sold for a profit.
sentences.zh: 磁带不能拿来牟利。

sentences.en: You had to either swap for another tape or simply give it away.
sentences.zh: 你只能拿它去换另一盘磁带，或者干脆免费送人。

sentences.en: The music was a communal resource to be shared freely.
sentences.zh: 音乐是一种供大家自由分享的公共资源。

sentences.en: The band came to understand that people were taping simply to enjoy the music, not to make a profit.
sentences.zh: 乐队逐渐理解到，人们录音纯粹是为了欣赏音乐，而不是为了赚钱。

sentences.en: They also realized the tapes acted as free advertising for their concerts.
sentences.zh: 他们也意识到磁带成了他们演唱会的免费广告。

sentences.en: And most importantly, they didn't want to be narcs.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，他们不想当告密者。

sentences.en: The earliest cassette recorders were still mono and lower fidelity.
sentences.zh: 最早的盒式录音机仍然是单声道的，音质较低。

sentences.en: But throughout the 1970s, new higher fidelity portable cassette decks were released, made by brands like Nakamichi and Sony.
sentences.zh: 但在整个70年代，中道和索尼等品牌推出了音质更好的全新便携式卡式录音座。

sentences.en: Some even came with microphones.
sentences.zh: 有些甚至还自带麦克风。

sentences.en: Taping became more and more accessible.
sentences.zh: 录音变得越来越触手可及。

sentences.en: Suddenly with cassettes, it really, all you had to do was pop it in the machine and hit record.
sentences.zh: 有了磁带，突然之间，你只需要把磁带塞进机器然后按录音键就行了。

sentences.en: There was almost nothing else to it.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有别的复杂要求。

sentences.en: As the cassette spread, so did dead tapes.
sentences.zh: 随着磁带的普及，感恩而死的磁带也随之传开。

sentences.en: When the band took a break from the road in the mid-1970s, the tapes kept circulating without them.
sentences.zh: 当乐队在70年代中期暂停巡演时，磁带依然在没有他们的情况下流传着。

sentences.en: By the end of the decade, the band was a cultural phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 到这个十年结束时，乐队已经成了一种文化现象。

sentences.en: Caravans of deadheads would drive around the country following them around from show to show.
sentences.zh: 死忠粉的车队开遍全国，一路追随着他们的每一场演出。

sentences.en: At that point, cassette decks had widely replaced eight tracks in cars.
sentences.zh: 到了那个时候，汽车里的磁带播放器已经全面取代了8轨磁带。

sentences.en: So as you drove from one show to the next, you could listen to your dead tapes the entire way.
sentences.zh: 所以当你从一场演出开车赶往下一场时，一路上都可以听着感恩而死的磁带。

sentences.en: The vibes never had to stop.
sentences.zh: 快乐的氛围永远不会停止。

sentences.en: Much like the dead's shows, every cassette was a little different.
sentences.zh: 就像感恩而死的演出一样，每一盘磁带有其独特之处。

sentences.en: There are two main types of recording, soundboard and audience.
sentences.zh: 录音主要分为两种类型：调音台录音和现场观众录音。

sentences.en: This is a soundboard recording.
sentences.zh: 这是一段调音台录音。

sentences.en: It's clear, tight, dry, very little crowd noise.
sentences.zh: 它清晰、紧凑、干燥，几乎没有什么观众的杂音。

sentences.en: These were recorded by the dead's road crew, though sometimes they'd provide a feed to friendly tapers.
sentences.zh: 这些是由感恩而死的巡演工作人员录制的，不过有时他们也会向友好的录音客提供音频源。

sentences.en: Some of these leaked out to the tape trading community, but most of them went into the archives and weren't heard until much later.
sentences.zh: 其中一些流传到了磁带交换圈子里，但大多数都进入了档案库，直到很久以后才被人听到。

sentences.en: Audience recordings were much more common.
sentences.zh: 现场观众录音要常见得多。

sentences.en: There's a lot less clarity, but you get more overall blend of the band, the room sound, and the audience.
sentences.zh: 清晰度要差很多，但你能听到乐队、空间音效和观众融为一体的综合效果。

sentences.en: This one was recorded at Bob's recommended 40 feet back.
sentences.zh: 这段录音是按照鲍勃推荐的后退40英尺的距离录制的。

sentences.en: I mean, this sounds pretty good, considering it's just a guy who stuck a tape deck down his pants and hoisted a mic up above the crowd.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，考虑到这只是一个人把录音机塞进裤子里、再把麦克风高高举过人群头顶录出来的，听起来相当不错。

sentences.en: In order to share the tapes widely, they would get copied.
sentences.zh: 为了让磁带广泛传播，人们会对它们进行复制。

sentences.en: Over and over.
sentences.zh: 一遍又一遍。

sentences.en: People would have dubbing parties where they'd all each bring a tape recorder and they'd chain them all together.
sentences.zh: 人们会举办翻录派对，每个人都带上录音机，把它们串联起来。

sentences.en: And later, dual deck cassette recorders could make copies without needing a second machine.
sentences.zh: 后来，双卡录音机不需要第二台机器就能直接复制。

sentences.en: But those copies didn't sound exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 但这些复制品听起来并不完全一样。

sentences.en: Every time you made a copy, you would reduce the fidelity of the tape further and further.
sentences.zh: 每次你制作一份复制品，磁带的保真度就会进一步降低。

sentences.en: The sound degrades a little bit more every time, and the tape hiss multiplies.
sentences.zh: 每复制一次，声音就会退化一点，磁带的嘶嘶声也会成倍增加。

sentences.en: That's called generation loss.
sentences.zh: 这被称为代际损失。

sentences.en: So a pristine first-generation soundboard recording
sentences.zh: 所以，原本原始的第一代调音台录音

sentences.en: Sounds much worse after being copied just three times.
sentences.zh: 在仅仅被复制三次后，听起来就要差得多了。

sentences.en: You can hear it's way noisier.
sentences.zh: 你能听出来噪声大了很多。

sentences.en: And if you copied it too many times, say ten, it gets pretty rough.
sentences.zh: 如果你复制太多次，比如说十次，声音就会变得相当糟糕。

sentences.en: The music gets buried in noise, and everything is all warbly.
sentences.zh: 音乐被噪声淹没，整段声音听起来都颤抖走音了。

sentences.en: Dead fans were willing to put up with these sonic drawbacks if it meant that they could listen to more Dead.
sentences.zh: 只要能听到更多的感恩而死音乐，歌迷们愿意忍受这些音质上的缺陷。

sentences.en: The sound even had an advantage over the official live albuMs.
sentences.zh: 这种声音甚至比官方现场专辑还有优势。

sentences.en: Cassettes became associated with sort of a more authentic experience in a weird way.
sentences.zh: 不知为何，磁带逐渐与一种更真实的体验联系在了一起。

sentences.en: It didn't go to some recording studio and get polished.
sentences.zh: 它没有送到什么录音室去精雕细琢。

sentences.en: It's just direct expression.
sentences.zh: 它就是直接的表达。

sentences.en: This isn't something that's being passed through a lot of gatekeepers.
sentences.zh: 这不是那种经过重重关卡层层筛选的东西。

sentences.en: All of this taping meant that deadheads could listen to virtually every single show.
sentences.zh: 所有这些录音意味着死忠粉可以听到几乎每一场演出。

sentences.en: It led to this kind of extreme scholarship.
sentences.zh: 这催生了一种极端考据的学术风气。

sentences.en: Sophie Hageny again.
sentences.zh: 又是苏菲·哈格尼。

sentences.en: There's a kind of obsession with, like, encyclopedic details.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种对百科全书般细节的狂热。

sentences.en: But I think that it's really boring to hear someone talk for six hours about some minor point of some keyboardist from 1989.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，听某个人喋喋不休地讲上六个小时关于1989年某位键盘手的某个微小细节，真的是无聊透顶。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, if I were a deadhead, this is exactly the type of deadhead I would be.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，如果我是个死忠粉，我绝对就是这种类型的死忠粉。

sentences.en: Die Hard fans didn't just listen to the music.
sentences.zh: 死忠歌迷不只是听音乐。

sentences.en: They collected it, organized it, and cataloged it.
sentences.zh: 他们收集音乐、整理音乐并将其编目。

sentences.en: Labeling cassettes became an art unto itself.
sentences.zh: 给磁带贴标签本身就成了一门艺术。

sentences.en: Fan magazines published set lists and had classified sections.
sentences.zh: 粉丝杂志会刊登歌单并设有分类广告栏。

sentences.en: Taper seeks tape.
sentences.zh: 录音客在寻找磁带。

sentences.en: I talked to the person who, by all accounts, has the single largest collection.
sentences.zh: 我采访了据各方公认拥有最大磁带收藏的人。

sentences.en: Mark Rodriguez, an artist who builds massive sculptures out of copies of dead cassettes.
sentences.zh: 马克·罗德里格斯，一位用废旧磁带的副本建造巨型雕塑的艺术家。

sentences.en: My collection is probably around 13,000 tapes or so.
sentences.zh: 我的收藏大概有13,000盘左右的磁带。

sentences.en: You know, that's going to be multiples or doubles and triples of certain shows.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其中会有某些特定演出的多个版本或双倍、三倍的重复。

sentences.en: The Dead channeled almost their entire artistic energy into their live shows.
sentences.zh: 感恩而死乐队几乎将他们全部的艺术精力都倾注在现场演出中。

sentences.en: These tapes make them perhaps the most documented artist across any medium.
sentences.zh: 这些磁带使他们成为各媒介中记录最详尽的艺术家。

sentences.en: Say if you had a video recording of Van Gogh visiting his studio every day and making his paintings and knowing exactly what brushes he used,
sentences.zh: 假设你有一段梵高每天去工作室作画、清楚知道他用了什么画笔的视频录像，

sentences.en: you'd be like, oh yeah, like when he painted Starry Night on such and such a date, he used that mongoose brush.
sentences.zh: 你就会觉得，哦对啊，就像他在某年某月某日画《星夜》时，用的是那支猫鼬毛画笔。

sentences.en: We see their development, we get all the hiccups, we get all the flubs, we get all the successes.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了他们的发展，我们经历了所有的磕磕绊绊，所有的失误，所有的成功。

sentences.en: Dead fans can debate about the best versions of songs or best eras of the band.
sentences.zh: 死忠歌迷可以争论歌曲的最佳版本或乐队的黄金时期。

sentences.en: But because everything was captured, people sometimes even have their favorite detritus.
sentences.zh: 但因为一切都被捕捉了下来，人们有时甚至连他们最喜欢的琐碎片段都有。

sentences.en: Sometimes you want to listen to a song and you don't want to listen to the part where they're like,
sentences.zh: 有时候你想听一首歌，但又不想听他们那种片段，比如，

sentences.en: oh, the guitar is not really working that well.
sentences.zh: 噢，这把吉他好像有点不太行。

sentences.en: But I think that's also part of it.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这也是其中一部分。

sentences.en: I like listening to Bob Weir talking about like how hot it is in Oregon,
sentences.zh: 我喜欢听鲍勃·韦尔谈论俄勒冈州的天气有多热，

sentences.en: that specific time out, like every time before it's been raining.
sentences.zh: 那种特定时间的闲聊，就像之前每一次都在下雨一样。

sentences.en: I don't know, this may be the first time I've ever been to Oregon, it didn't rain, now it's too damn hot.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，这可能是我这辈子第一次来俄勒冈州没下雨，结果现在热得要死。

sentences.en: It wasn't like Bob's off-the-cuff comment about the weather was meant to like live forever, and yet it kind of does.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃关于天气的随口评论并不是为了流传百世，然而它某种程度上确实流传下来了。

sentences.en: I don't think the band expected that half a century later, people would be listening to their tuning and stage announcements.
sentences.zh: 我想乐队绝不会料到，半个世纪后人们还会听他们调音和报幕。

sentences.en: Jonathan D.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·D·

sentences.en: Stevens of Boston University, 036369705, valid only with current label.
sentences.zh: 史蒂芬，波士顿大学，036369705，仅在当前标签有效。

sentences.en: Your wallet is up here.
sentences.zh: 你的钱包在这里。

sentences.en: But people weren't just listening to the tapes for the music.
sentences.zh: 但人们听磁带不只是为了听音乐。

sentences.en: It was a way of carrying the atmosphere of a dead show into your everyday life.
sentences.zh: 这是将“感恩而死”演唱会的氛围带入日常生活的一种方式。

sentences.en: The tapes were kind of a hang.
sentences.zh: 这些磁带就像是一场聚会。

sentences.en: Fast forward to the early 1980s.
sentences.zh: 快进到20世纪80年代初。

sentences.en: Cassette sales had finally overtaken vinyl.
sentences.zh: 磁带销量终于超过了黑胶唱片。

sentences.en: The newly introduced Walkman created the power to soundtrack your life at all times.
sentences.zh: 新推出的随身听让你随时随地都能为生活配乐。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the dead were bigger than ever.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，“感恩而死”乐队比以往任何时候都更加火爆。

sentences.en: They chose to fully focus on touring and went seven years without releasing a studio album.
sentences.zh: 他们选择全力专注于巡演，有七年没有发行录音室专辑。

sentences.en: Even casual fans were mainly listening to the tapes.
sentences.zh: 甚至连普通歌迷也主要在听磁带。

sentences.en: That was the only place to hear new songs outside of a concert.
sentences.zh: 那是演唱会之外听到新歌的唯一途径。

sentences.en: But there was a problem.
sentences.zh: 但有个问题。

sentences.en: Some of these tapers were driving other fans nuts.
sentences.zh: 其中一些录音客把其他歌迷逼疯了。

sentences.en: Another person they were driving nuts was Dan Healy, the Grateful Dead's longtime sound engineer.
sentences.zh: 另一个让他们抓狂的人是丹·希利，“感恩而死”乐队长期的音响师。

sentences.en: He told the story in a 1989 interview.
sentences.zh: 他在1989年的一次采访中讲述了这段经历。

sentences.en: Tapers got an inflated version of their own importance for a while there.
sentences.zh: 那段时间里，录音客对自己的重要性产生了过高的估计。

sentences.en: They were beginning to lean on non-tapers who had seats that they wanted and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们开始向非录音客施压，抢占别人想要座位之类的好位置。

sentences.en: One thing led to another in the concept of the tapers section.
sentences.zh: 种种原因促成了设立录音客专区的概念。

sentences.en: It was like either band taping altogether or organizing.
sentences.zh: 要么就索性全面禁止录音，要么就得好好组织一下。

sentences.en: So in October of 1984, the band set up an official tapers section.
sentences.zh: 所以在1984年10月，乐队设立了一个官方的录音客专区。

sentences.en: Tapers would buy special tickets to sit behind Healy,
sentences.zh: 录音客会买特价票坐在希利身后，

sentences.en: where they wouldn't bother the other fans who simply wanted to listen and vibe in peace.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就不会打扰到那些只想安安静静听歌、感受氛围的其他歌迷了。

sentences.en: At that point, the band's finances were dire.
sentences.zh: 当时，乐队的财务状况极其糟糕。

sentences.en: For their entire career, they'd struggled to break even.
sentences.zh: 在他们的整个职业生涯中，他们一直在艰难地收支平衡。

sentences.en: Their ticket sales were massive, but so was their overhead.
sentences.zh: 他们的门票收入巨大，但管理费用也同样高昂。

sentences.en: They started considering their tape vault as a potential source of income.
sentences.zh: 他们开始将他们的磁带库视为潜在的收入来源。

sentences.en: So they hired a prolific tape collector to help them sift through the archives.
sentences.zh: 于是他们雇佣了一位多产的磁带收藏家来帮他们整理档案。

sentences.en: Hi, my name's Dick Latvala, and welcome to the Grateful Dead vault.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫迪克·拉特瓦拉，欢迎来到“感恩而死”乐队的档案库。

sentences.en: In 1974, I started collecting tapes, and then I did nothing else for about 10 years.
sentences.zh: 1974年，我开始收集磁带，然后在大约10年的时间里什么都没做。

sentences.en: Dick Latvala had struck up a friendship with the band and the crew over the years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，迪克·拉特瓦拉与乐队和工作人员结下了深厚的友谊。

sentences.en: Sometimes they'd slip him copies of soundboard recordings.
sentences.zh: 有时他们会偷偷塞给他一些调音台录音的副本。

sentences.en: He and other tapers had long advocated for official releases of these tapes,
sentences.zh: 他和别的录音客长期以来一直主张官方发行这些磁带，

sentences.en: but the band always thought they were too lo-fi to put out.
sentences.zh: 但乐队总觉得它们的音质太粗糙，拿不上台面。

sentences.en: Eventually, they came around.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们改变了主意。

sentences.en: In 1993, they released the first CD of the Dick's Pick series, which was an instant success.
sentences.zh: 1993年，他们发行了“迪克的精选”系列的第一张CD，获得了巨大成功。

sentences.en: The advertising played up the rawness of the tapes,
sentences.zh: 广告大肆宣传磁带的原始粗粝感，

sentences.en: recognizing that fans had come to see it as a virtue.
sentences.zh: 意识到歌迷已经开始将其视为一种美德。

sentences.en: By 1991, CDs replaced cassettes as the most popular format.
sentences.zh: 到1991年，CD取代磁带成为最受欢迎的格式。

sentences.en: Many tapers had also switched to digital recorders, but those were much more expensive,
sentences.zh: 许多录音客也转向了数字录音机，但那些设备要昂贵得多，

sentences.en: and CD-R burners cost thousands of dollars at the time.
sentences.zh: 而且当时刻录CD-R需要花几千美元。

sentences.en: The easiest way to share the recordings from fan to fan was still the cassette.
sentences.zh: 歌迷之间分享录音最简单的方式依然是磁带。

sentences.en: Jerry Garcia, the lead guitarist and co-founder of the band known as the Grateful Dead,
sentences.zh: 杰里·加西亚，被称为“感恩而死”乐队的主音吉他手兼联合创始人，

sentences.en: died today, reportedly of natural causes.
sentences.zh: 于今天逝世，据报道死于自然原因。

sentences.en: He was 53 years old.
sentences.zh: 享年53岁。

sentences.en: He'd been in precarious...
sentences.zh: 他的身体状况一直不太稳定……

sentences.en: The Grateful Dead split up in 1995 after Jerry Garcia's death.
sentences.zh: 1995年杰里·加西亚逝世后，“感恩而死”乐队解散了。

sentences.en: But the story doesn't end there.
sentences.zh: 但故事并没有就此结束。

sentences.en: Similar taping networks sprung up around other bands.
sentences.zh: 类似的录音网络在其他乐队周围如雨后春笋般涌现。

sentences.en: Dead tapes continued to circulate,
sentences.zh: “感恩而死”的磁带仍在流传，

sentences.en: and tapers still followed around the Dead's offshoots and solo projects.
sentences.zh: 录音客们依然追随着“感恩而死”的分支乐队和个人项目。

sentences.en: Deadheads congregated and communicated on the internet,
sentences.zh: 死忠迷在互联网上聚集和交流，

sentences.en: which they'd been doing since, well, the invention of the internet.
sentences.zh: 他们从，嗯，互联网发明之初就一直在这么做了。

sentences.en: Their early home base was close to the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Lab,
sentences.zh: 他们早期的根据地靠近斯坦福人工智能实验室，

sentences.en: where many early internet protocols were developed.
sentences.zh: 许多早期互联网协议就是在那里开发的。

sentences.en: The lab was full of deadheads, and the band would sometimes drop by, too.
sentences.zh: 实验室里到处都是“感恩而死”的死忠，乐队有时也会顺道拜访。

sentences.en: One of the lab's first uses of email was to organize outings to dead shows.
sentences.zh: 该实验室最早使用电子邮件的用途之一，就是组织去观看“感恩而死”的演出。

sentences.en: As the internet slowly developed, deadheads were there every step of the way,
sentences.zh: 随着互联网的慢慢发展，死忠迷们在每一步都没有缺席，

sentences.en: from 1980s Usenet groups to AOL keyword dead.
sentences.zh: 从20世纪80年代的Usenet群组到AOL的死忠关键词。

sentences.en: They were using the internet to connect,
sentences.zh: 他们用互联网来建立联系，

sentences.en: but they still had to trade tapes and CDRs by mail.
sentences.zh: 但他们仍然必须通过邮寄方式交换磁带和CDR。

sentences.en: But it wasn't long before all physical media was rendered more or less obsolete by the MP3.
sentences.zh: 但没过多久，所有的物理媒介在MP3面前都变得或多或少过时了。

sentences.en: In the early 2000s, fans embarked on a collective project to digitize and organize the recordings,
sentences.zh: 20世纪2000年代初，歌迷们发起了一项集体项目，将录音数字化并分类，

sentences.en: which found a home on archive.org.
sentences.zh: 这些内容在archive.org找到了归宿。

sentences.en: Deadheads no longer had to cultivate their own personal libraries
sentences.zh: “感恩而死”的死忠们再也不用苦心经营自己的个人藏书，

sentences.en: or track down rare recordings themselves.
sentences.zh: 或者自己去搜寻稀有录音了。

sentences.en: With one click, they could pull up virtually any moment from the dead's entire history.
sentences.zh: 只需轻轻一按，他们就能调出乐队整个历史上的几乎任何一个瞬间。

sentences.en: And if they had a tape that was missing, they could share it with the rest of the fandom.
sentences.zh: 如果他们有什么漏掉的磁带，他们可以与整个粉丝群体分享。

sentences.en: The Walkman couldn't compete with the iPod.
sentences.zh: 随身听无法与iPod竞争。

sentences.en: The cassette simply wasn't useful anymore.
sentences.zh: 磁带彻底失去了用武之地。

sentences.en: And so people started getting rid of them.
sentences.zh: 于是人们开始处理掉它们。

sentences.en: The tapes are literally kind of worthless.
sentences.zh: 这些磁带简直可以说是毫无价值。

sentences.en: The value that they hold is really only sentimental.
sentences.zh: 它们承载的价值其实只有情怀。

sentences.en: And for people who possess this particular obsession,
sentences.zh: 对于有这种特殊执念的人来说，

sentences.en: they function more like literal memories, like souvenirs, than as collector's iteMs.
sentences.zh: 它们与其说是收藏品，不如说是具象化的记忆，就像纪念品一样。

sentences.en: 2023 saw the last shows by the final incarnation of the Grateful Dead.
sentences.zh: 2023年迎来了“感恩而死”最后化身的最后几场演出。

sentences.en: Dead and company featured a couple of original members,
sentences.zh: “死与公司”由几位元老级成员组成，

sentences.en: plus some other jam band veterans,
sentences.zh: 加上一些其他的即兴乐队老兵，

sentences.en: and your body is a Wonderland singer,
sentences.zh: 还有演唱《你的身体是个仙境》的歌手

sentences.en: John Mayer, standing in for Jerry Garcia.
sentences.zh: 约翰·梅尔，代替了杰里·加西亚的位置。

sentences.en: There were still tapers,
sentences.zh: 现场依然有录音客，

sentences.en: but now fans could live stream professional recordings of every show.
sentences.zh: 但现在歌迷可以观看每场演出的专业录音直播。

sentences.en: Taping was no longer a necessity, but more of a hobby.
sentences.zh: 录音不再是一种必需品，而更像是一种业余爱好。

sentences.en: Sophie saw Dead & Co.
sentences.zh: 苏菲看过“死与公司”的

sentences.en: many times,
sentences.zh: 很多场演出，

sentences.en: including their July farewell shows in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 包括他们7月份在旧金山的告别演出。

sentences.en: The culture of going to like a massive stadium dead show
sentences.zh: 那种去观看大型体育场级别的“感恩而死”演唱会的文化，

sentences.en: that includes like original members of the band,
sentences.zh: 其中还包括乐队的创始成员，

sentences.en: that feels like it's ending.
sentences.zh: 感觉它正在走向终结。

sentences.en: I can't really see what replaces that.
sentences.zh: 我实在想象不出有什么能取代它。

sentences.en: And that's really sad.
sentences.zh: 这真的很让人难过。

sentences.en: Like, I think, I'm like, what will I do next summer?
sentences.zh: 比如说，我在想，我明年夏天该做什么呢？

sentences.en: Sophie is not the taper type.
sentences.zh: 苏菲可不是那种会录音的歌迷。

sentences.en: But of course, she did have her phone.
sentences.zh: 但当然，她确实带着手机。

sentences.en: Phone cameras have turned us into a culture of compulsive documentation.
sentences.zh: 手机摄像头把我们变成了一种强迫性记录的文化。

sentences.en: Simply because it's so easy.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为这太容易了。

sentences.en: I asked Sophie if she had any videos from that last show.
sentences.zh: 我问苏菲她有没有最后那场演出的视频。

sentences.en: I actually did not take very many phone videos,
sentences.zh: 我其实没拍多少手机视频，

sentences.en: but I did, you know, I have some.
sentences.zh: 不过我确实，你知道的，我有一些。

sentences.en: So let me just see what I have.
sentences.zh: 所以让我看看我都有什么。

sentences.en: They weren't exactly Cornell 77.
sentences.zh: 它们可算不上什么“康奈尔77”。

sentences.en: All my videos are like six seconds long and low quality.
sentences.zh: 我所有的视频都只有大约六秒长，而且画质很渣。

sentences.en: Okay, you can't even really, that's fire in the mountain.
sentences.zh: 好了，你甚至都看不清，那是《山中烈火》。

sentences.en: Let's see, what do we get here?
sentences.zh: 让我看看，我们这儿有什么？

sentences.en: So there you go.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: She told me the clips were so short because she kept having a sudden realization.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，这些短片之所以这么短，是因为她脑海里一直闪现出一个突如其来的感悟。

sentences.en: It's a familiar feeling to me and probably to you too.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉对我来说很熟悉，对你来说大概也是如此。

sentences.en: You're having a great experience.
sentences.zh: 你正在经历一段美妙的体验。

sentences.en: So you pull out your phone and take a photo or video.
sentences.zh: 于是你掏出手机拍照或录像。

sentences.en: Maybe you even post it right away.
sentences.zh: 也许你甚至马上就发到了网上。

sentences.en: But then you realize, now I'm just looking at my phone.
sentences.zh: 但随后你意识到，现在我只是在盯着手机看。

sentences.en: Documenting and sharing is so easy that it's become our new default.
sentences.zh: 记录和分享是如此简单，以至于它成了我们的新默认习惯。

sentences.en: But this old man is going to shake his fist at a cloud right now and tell you
sentences.zh: 但这个老头现在要对着云挥舞拳头，告诉你

sentences.en: there is no way around it.
sentences.zh: 这是无可奈何的。

sentences.en: Capturing a moment makes it harder to be in the moment.
sentences.zh: 捕捉一个瞬间会让人更难置身于那个瞬间之中。

sentences.en: Dead cassettes are an artifact of when recording was rare and sharing took work.
sentences.zh: “感恩而死”的磁带是录音罕见、分享需要付出努力的时代产物。

sentences.en: Tapers were volunteering on behalf of Deadhead's past, present, and future
sentences.zh: 录音客们代表着过去、现在和未来的死忠迷们自愿行动，

sentences.en: to try and capture every fleeting moment.
sentences.zh: 试图捕捉每一个稍纵即逝的时刻。

sentences.en: To capture the entire moment.
sentences.zh: 捕捉整个时刻。

sentences.en: Not just the music, but the feeling of being there.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是音乐，还有身临其境的感觉。

sentences.en: The music.
sentences.zh: 音乐。

sentences.en: There's one place where cassettes are still the most useful format for music.
sentences.zh: 有一个地方，磁带仍然是音乐最有用的格式。

sentences.en: We'll take you there after the break.
sentences.zh: 我们将在片花之后带大家去看看。

sentences.en: Back in 2016, we ran a story about a place where cassettes remain the most useful format.
sentences.zh: 早在2016年，我们就报道过一个磁带依然是最实用格式的地方。

sentences.en: Documentarian Alex Lambert takes us there.
sentences.zh: 纪录片导演亚历克斯·兰伯特将带我们前往那里。

sentences.en: The United States prison system has the largest prison population in the world.
sentences.zh: 美国的监狱系统拥有世界上最多的囚犯人口。

sentences.en: And when the more than two million prisoners in this country have access to music,
sentences.zh: 当这个国家两百万多的囚犯能够接触到音乐时，

sentences.en: it's often on cassette.
sentences.zh: 通常都是通过磁带。

sentences.en: Well, my number one thing to keep around here is my walkman, my tapes, my legal papers, and some bottle of water.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在这里最离不开的东西是我的随身听、我的磁带、我的法律文件以及一些瓶装水。

sentences.en: Yeah, they can have everything else.
sentences.zh: 对，他们可以保留其他所有东西。

sentences.en: That's Adolfo Davis.
sentences.zh: 那是阿道夫·戴维斯。

sentences.en: At 14 years old, he was involved in a gang-related shooting.
sentences.zh: 14岁时，他卷入了一起帮派枪击案。

sentences.en: He was tried as an adult and sentenced to life in prison.
sentences.zh: 他被以成年人身份审判，并被判处终身监禁。

sentences.en: Adolfo is 39 now, and he's serving his sentence at Stateville Correctional Center in Illinois.
sentences.zh: 阿道夫现在39岁，目前在伊利诺伊州的斯泰特维尔惩教中心服刑。

sentences.en: Listening to music on tapes is one of his only means of escape.
sentences.zh: 用磁带听音乐是他仅有的精神寄托之一。

sentences.en: That's the only way I think I've made it so far because I have a good imagination.
sentences.zh: 我想我能坚持到今天全靠这个，因为我有很好的想象力。

sentences.en: And I'd just close my eyes, put my earbuds in, and I'd just be gone.
sentences.zh: 我只要闭上眼睛，塞上耳机，整个人就仿佛置身别处了。

sentences.en: In 1990, the year Adolfo was incarcerated, everybody was listening to music on cassette tapes.
sentences.zh: 1990年，也就是阿道夫入狱的那一年，大家都用磁带听音乐。

sentences.en: In fact, Adolfo had some with him when he went to prison.
sentences.zh: 事实上，阿道夫入狱时身上就带了几盘磁带。

sentences.en: Yeah, I got locked up with a walkman and I think like seven tapes.
sentences.zh: 对，我进去的时候带了一个随身听，还有大概七盘磁带吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, when I was used to sell drugs, I'd have a fanny pack.
sentences.zh: 对，我以前卖毒品的时候，会系一个腰包。

sentences.en: And I'd have my walkman in my fanny pack with my tapes.
sentences.zh: 我的随身听和磁带就放在腰包里。

sentences.en: And I'd be listening to the walkman while I'm watching out for security for the police.
sentences.zh: 我一边帮警察……不对，一边帮他们放哨防范安保人员，一边听着随身听。

sentences.en: A fanny pack.
sentences.zh: 一个腰包。

sentences.en: We usually call it a couch, but it's a fanny pack.
sentences.zh: 我们通常叫它“屁股包”，不过它确实是个腰包。

sentences.en: Let's be real.
sentences.zh: 说实话吧。

sentences.en: Just a few years after Adolfo was locked up,
sentences.zh: 就在阿道夫入狱几年后，

sentences.en: the cassette tape would be all but replaced by the CD out here in the free world.
sentences.zh: 在自由世界的我们这里，盒式磁带差点就被CD完全取代了。

sentences.en: But in prison, the cassette lived on.
sentences.zh: 但在监狱里，磁带却延续了下来。

sentences.en: I'd be telling my family, like, I need to order a tape.
sentences.zh: 我会告诉家人：“我需要订购一盘磁带。”

sentences.en: And the younger generation that I'd be talking to, they don't even know what a tape is.
sentences.zh: 而我对话的那些年轻人，甚至都不知道磁带是什么。

sentences.en: And not just any old cassette tape is allowed in prison.
sentences.zh: 而且并不是随便什么旧磁带都能带进监狱的。

sentences.en: Some prisons require a very specific type of cassette tape.
sentences.zh: 有些监狱对磁带有非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: It has to be clear.
sentences.zh: 它必须是透明的。

sentences.en: It has to be sonically welded so it can't be taken apart and put back together.
sentences.zh: 它必须是超声波焊接的，这样就无法拆开再装回去。

sentences.en: And the box it goes in has to also be perfectly clear.
sentences.zh: 装磁带的盒子也必须完全透明。

sentences.en: That's Steve Stepp, owner of National Audio Company, America's preeminent manufacturer of cassette tapes.
sentences.zh: 那是史蒂夫·斯泰普，美国卓越的磁带制造商——国家音频公司的老板。

sentences.en: The reason you can't have a five-screw cassette or maybe a colored cassette that's opaque
sentences.zh: 你不能用五颗螺丝的磁带，或者那种不透明的彩色磁带，

sentences.en: is they don't want a razor blade or narcotics or something else to be enclosed in a cassette.
sentences.zh: 原因在于监狱不希望磁带里藏有剃须刀片、毒品或其他东西。

sentences.en: They do have people in the correctional facilities who look at and inspect incoming materials
sentences.zh: 惩教设施里确实有人负责检查和审核运入的物资，

sentences.en: and they have to be able to see through or they won't allow them in.
sentences.zh: 他们必须能一眼看透，否则绝不放行。

sentences.en: Steve has gotten familiar with this subfield of cassette tape manufacturing
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫对磁带制造的这个细分领域已经非常熟悉，

sentences.en: even though it is not the focus of his business.
sentences.zh: 尽管这并不是他业务的核心。

sentences.en: Mostly he makes normal cassette tapes for a number of different markets.
sentences.zh: 他主要为各种不同的市场生产普通磁带。

sentences.en: Music labels, spoken word, audiobooks.
sentences.zh: 音乐唱片公司、有声读物、有声书。

sentences.en: Steve's factory in Springfield, Missouri produces both blank tapes
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫位于密苏里州斯普林菲尔德的工厂既生产空白磁带，

sentences.en: and tapes with audio already on them.
sentences.zh: 也生产已经录好音频的磁带。

sentences.en: Machines collate all those parts together, transfer them across on a conveyor
sentences.zh: 机器将所有零件组装在一起，通过传送带运送，

sentences.en: and then wrap them with cellophane and put a tear strip in.
sentences.zh: 然后用玻璃纸包装并贴上易撕条。

sentences.en: Steve was one of the first people in the cassette industry.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫是磁带行业最早的从业者之一。

sentences.en: And he's one of the only people still in it.
sentences.zh: 也是为数不多至今仍在坚守的人。

sentences.en: We're the only people I know of.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，我们是唯一还在做这行的。

sentences.en: Most of the people left in the cassette industry are mom-and-pop shops or small operations.
sentences.zh: 磁带行业里剩下的绝大多数都是夫妻店或小型作坊。

sentences.en: If you purchased a cassette recently from anywhere,
sentences.zh: 如果你最近在任何地方买过磁带，

sentences.en: from Radio Shack or from the merch table of some punk band you just saw live,
sentences.zh: 无论是从Radio Shack买的，还是从你刚看过的某个朋克乐队的周边摊位买的，

sentences.en: it probably started out in Steve's factory.
sentences.zh: 它很可能最初都产自史蒂夫的工厂。

sentences.en: His company ships out up to 100,000 cassettes a day.
sentences.zh: 他的公司每天发货多达10万盘磁带。

sentences.en: And a small number of those cassettes are special orders for prisoners,
sentences.zh: 其中有一小部分是专门为囚犯定制的订单，

sentences.en: made with clear plastic and without screws.
sentences.zh: 采用透明塑料材质，且没有螺丝。

sentences.en: Once the tapes leave here, we don't really see where they end up.
sentences.zh: 磁带一旦离开这里，我们就很难知道它们的最终去向了。

sentences.en: That's a part of the business that we can't see from where we are.
sentences.zh: 这是我们身处此地所无法触及的业务领域。

sentences.en: As for why cassettes have stuck around in prisons all these years,
sentences.zh: 至于为什么磁带能在监狱里历经多年而不衰，

sentences.en: it's hard to get a definitive answer because every prison is different.
sentences.zh: 很难得到一个确切的答案，因为每所监狱的情况都不一样。

sentences.en: But there's one theory we heard from a few different people.
sentences.zh: 但我们从不同的人那里听到过一种理论。

sentences.en: Tapes are allowed because CDs are easier to weaponize.
sentences.zh: 之所以允许磁带存在，是因为CD更容易被制作成武器。

sentences.en: They say that it's the most safest way for them to listen to music
sentences.zh: 他们说，听音乐用这种方式最安全，

sentences.en: because a CD you could break and maybe cut somebody with.
sentences.zh: 因为CD可以被砸碎，也许能用来割伤别人。

sentences.en: That's Chris Barrett.
sentences.zh: 那是克里斯·巴雷特。

sentences.en: This tape of him was recorded a couple years ago for a short film.
sentences.zh: 这段关于他的录音是几年前为一部短片拍摄的。

sentences.en: Chris used to run a service that helped families send packages to people in prison in New York State.
sentences.zh: 克里斯曾经经营一家服务机构，帮助纽约州的家属给狱中的亲人寄送包裹。

sentences.en: He had a warehouse full of items that had already been approved by the prison authorities.
sentences.zh: 他的仓库里堆满了已经获得监狱当局批准的物品。

sentences.en: Everything from food, clothing, boxer shorts, and, yeah, cassettes instead of CDs.
sentences.zh: 应有尽有，包括食品、衣物、平角内裤，还有——没错，是磁带而不是CD。

sentences.en: But he never really understood the logic behind it.
sentences.zh: 但他始终搞不懂这背后的逻辑。

sentences.en: They let me sell tuna fish cans that, you know, you pull off the top and that thing is metal.
sentences.zh: 他们允许我卖金枪鱼罐头，你知道的，拉开盖子那部分是金属的。

sentences.en: Like, it's much more dangerous than a CD, is my point, the tuna fish can than a CD.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，金枪鱼罐头比CD危险得多，真的。

sentences.en: So I don't know why they come up with some of the rules that they come up with.
sentences.zh: 所以我搞不懂他们为什么会制定出那样的一些规矩。

sentences.en: We just try to stay within those guidelines.
sentences.zh: 我们只能尽量遵守这些准则。

sentences.en: Chris, whose package sending service recently went out of business, also sold a lot of cassette Walkmans.
sentences.zh: 克里斯的包裹寄送服务最近刚刚倒闭，他也曾售卖过大量卡带随身听。

sentences.en: Walkmans used to be available for purchase in prison commissaries, but they generally aren't anymore,
sentences.zh: 随身听以前可以在监狱的小卖部买到，但现在通常买不到了，

sentences.en: which makes them extremely coveted iteMs.
sentences.zh: 这使得它们成了极其抢手的物件。

sentences.en: Like, if my Walkman breaks, I'm out of there.
sentences.zh: 如果我的随身听坏了，我就彻底完蛋了。

sentences.en: So I take good care of it.
sentences.zh: 所以我格外爱惜它。

sentences.en: Because if it breaks, it, like, I start crying.
sentences.zh: 因为如果它坏了，我会当场急哭的。

sentences.en: And wear and tear is not the only threat to the life of a Walkman.
sentences.zh: 而且日常磨损并不是随身听面临的唯一威胁。

sentences.en: But when it's like a major shakedown and they bring other officers from other institutions,
sentences.zh: 每当进行重大突击搜查、从其他监狱调来大批警员时，

sentences.en: they will just break your TV, break your radio, take your TV, take your radio, take your cassette tape.
sentences.zh: 他们会直接砸碎你的电视、砸碎你的收音机，没收你的电视、没收你的收音机、没收你的磁带。

sentences.en: Once you destroy my Walkman, I cannot get another Walkman.
sentences.zh: 一旦你毁了我的随身听，我就再也弄不到第二个了。

sentences.en: It's probably one of the most prized items for, you know, for theft.
sentences.zh: 它绝对是最容易招致盗窃的目标物品之一。

sentences.en: People try to, you know, try to hold on to them as much as they can.
sentences.zh: 大家都在千方百计地想要保住它们。

sentences.en: That's Efren Paredes, Jr.
sentences.zh: 那是小埃夫伦·帕雷德斯。

sentences.en: He was a 15-year-old honor student when he was tried as an adult on a murder charge
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名15岁的荣誉优等生，却因谋杀指控被当作成年人审判，

sentences.en: and sentenced to life without parole.
sentences.zh: 并被判处不得假释的终身监禁。

sentences.en: He's always maintained his innocence.
sentences.zh: 他一直坚称自己是无辜的。

sentences.en: Efren is 43 now, and during his 28 years in prison, he amassed a pretty big collection of music.
sentences.zh: 埃夫伦现在43岁了，在服刑的28年里，他积攒了相当大的一批音乐收藏。

sentences.en: Kendrick Lamar.
sentences.zh: 肯德里克·拉马尔。

sentences.en: I like Young Jeezy, Rick Ross, Meek Mills.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢杨·吉齐、里克·罗斯、米克·米尔。

sentences.en: I like Lil Wayne.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢莉尔·韦恩。

sentences.en: At Muskegon Correctional Facility in Michigan, where Efren is serving his sentence,
sentences.zh: 在埃夫伦服刑的密歇根州马斯凯根惩教中心，

sentences.en: prisoners can actually have MP3 players.
sentences.zh: 囚犯其实是可以拥有MP3播放器的。

sentences.en: Inmates can purchase an MP3 player through the prison commissary and then download music to it
sentences.zh: 服刑人员可以通过监狱小卖部购买MP3播放器，然后通过一家名为“接入娱乐”的公司提供的自助终端机下载音乐。

sentences.en: through a kiosk provided by a company called Access Entertainment.
sentences.zh: 通过一家名为“接入娱乐”的公司提供的自助终端机下载音乐。

sentences.en: Before downloading, they have to transfer money to the company and receive a credit for a certain amount of songs.
sentences.zh: 在下载之前，他们必须向该公司转账，并获得相应金额的歌曲下载额度。

sentences.en: But there's a catch.
sentences.zh: 但这里有个限制。

sentences.en: In Michigan, there's a policy that they try to restrict as much music that would be labeled as parental advisory.
sentences.zh: 在密歇根州有一项政策，他们试图尽可能限制那些被贴上“家长指引”标签的音乐。

sentences.en: In other words, the state of Michigan will try and sentence a 15-year-old as an adult,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，密歇根州试图把一个15岁的孩子当作成年人判刑，

sentences.en: but when he becomes an actual adult, the state won't let him purchase music deemed inappropriate for a teenager.
sentences.zh: 但当他真正成为成年人时，州政府却不让他购买被认为不适合青少年的音乐。

sentences.en: It's interesting that, you know, the Department of Corrections has never taken any steps to restricting.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，惩教部门从未采取任何实质步骤去进行限制。

sentences.en: We couldn't confirm that there were no restrictions on cassette music, but Efren hasn't encountered them.
sentences.zh: 我们无法证实磁带音乐是否完全不受限制，但埃夫伦确实没遇到过。

sentences.en: And that's why he says a lot of inmates still prefer cassettes.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，他说许多囚犯仍然更偏爱磁带。

sentences.en: They listen to them all the time, on their personal Walkmans and sometimes out loud.
sentences.zh: 他们随时随地都在听，用自己的随身听，有时还外放出来。

sentences.en: Actually, as we're talking right now, there's a gentleman in the bathroom washing clothes with his radio on, playing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，就在我们交谈的此时此刻，卫生间里就有一位先生开着收音机在洗衣服。

sentences.en: Right underneath the part of the prison where Efren is locked up is the wing that houses the prisoners in solitary confinement.
sentences.zh: 在埃夫伦被关押的监狱区域正下方，就是关押单人禁闭囚犯的侧翼。

sentences.en: We hear guys all the time yelling up to us saying, hey, turn the music on, turn some music on.
sentences.zh: 我们经常听到那里的伙计们朝上面大喊：嘿，把音乐打开，放点音乐吧。

sentences.en: You know, turn on, turn Rick Ross on or turn on Meek Mill or...
sentences.zh: 你知道的，放点儿音乐，放首里克·罗斯或者米克·米尔，或者……

sentences.en: Ain't this what they've been waiting for?
sentences.zh: 这不正是他们一直期盼的吗？

sentences.en: You know, something so that they can hear down there something that's, you know, music from upstairs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，弄出点动静让他们在下面能听到，能听到来自楼上的音乐。

sentences.en: Prisons tend to be late adopters of technology.
sentences.zh: 监狱往往是科技发展的滞后者。

sentences.en: So maybe one day all prisons in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以也许有一天，全美所有的监狱

sentences.en: will just make the switch from cassette to digital.
sentences.zh: 都会从磁带全面过渡到数字格式。

sentences.en: Or maybe they'll go to CDs first, just to be illogically chronological.
sentences.zh: 或者他们也可能先过渡到CD，来个不合逻辑的逆向演变。

sentences.en: Whatever the format, the most important thing about music to Efren and Adolfo is escape and connection.
sentences.zh: 不管是什么格式，对埃夫伦和阿道夫来说，音乐最重要的意义在于逃离现实与心灵连结。

sentences.en: Here's Adolfo again.
sentences.zh: 下面有请阿道夫再次发言。

sentences.en: Music connects us all together.
sentences.zh: 音乐把我们所有人紧紧连结在一起。

sentences.en: Everybody shares music with each other.
sentences.zh: 每个人都与他人分享音乐。

sentences.en: You know, music allows everyone to escape from this place.
sentences.zh: 你知道，音乐让每个人都能从这个地方逃离出去。

sentences.en: I can't, I can't do it without my music.
sentences.zh: 我不能，没有音乐我简直活不下去。

sentences.en: In the days I rest my Walkman, I bought a Walkman for somebody else to listen to their Walkman before I can go to the street.
sentences.zh: 在我让随身听“休息”的日子里，我买了一个随身听借给别人听，好在我重获自由前让他们也有音乐可听。

sentences.en: The days that you don't have your Walkman?
sentences.zh: 那些没有随身听的日子怎么办？

sentences.en: No, like, I play my Walkman like three days, then I let it rest like two days.
sentences.zh: 不，我是说，我用随身听听三天，然后让它休息两天。

sentences.en: He rests his Walkman.
sentences.zh: 他让他的随身听休息。

sentences.en: That is love.
sentences.zh: 这就是爱。
